newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends at record low close.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends at record low close.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index lost 0.165 points or 0.35 percent to end at a record low close of 46.478 points on Thursday.
In intra-day trading, the index hit an all-time low of 46.436 points, toppling the former historical low of 46.652 points set on Wednesday.
Trading was slow with most investors staying on the sidelines due to weak market sentiment, traders said.
Combined volume was 6.8 million shares worth $2.7 million. Of 41 B shares, 34 traded, with 13 down, five flat and 16 up.

Brokers said that, after the index hit a record low on Wednesday, more foreign investors liquidated their positions today and late bargain-hunting from domestic investors failed to prevent the index from falling further.
"In late trading today, domestic individuals bought shares on bargain-hunting, but their influence was too weak to resist selling from overseas investors," one trader said.

"If there is no concrete support from the central government, the market's downward trend is unlikely to be reversed in the short term," a second broker said. "It is hard to say now where lies the bottom line for the index."

Shanghai Posts and Telecommunications Equipment was the day's biggest loser on market rumours that its 1996 results will be poorer than expected, brokers said. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
The stock fell $0.028 or 8.58 percent to $0.298, on volume of 200,000 shares.

Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the second loser, falling $0.040 or 6.89 percent to $0.540, on volume of 327,000 shares. Brokers said its warrants on a rights issue currently traded on the bourse were not selling well, depressing investor confidence.
Shanghai New Asia traded the most on inter-institutional trading, ending flat at $0.476, on volume of 924,000 shares.
Shanghai's A share index ended up on a technical rebound after successive falls since late last week.
Brokers said most investors were cautious with the short-term market trend uncertain on persistent rumours that the securities authorities would crack down on the market.

The A index closed up 14.127 points or 1.47 percent to 976.626 points, on volume of 310.6 million shares worth 2.9 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index put on 24.944 points or 1.04 percent to 2434.147 points.
Qilianshan Cement was the star performer on a newspaper report its profits rose sharply this year. It jumped 0.90 yuan or 10.00 percent to 9.90 yuan on volume of 1.1 million shares.
The Shanghai Securities News said the firm's net profits rose by a year-on-year 45 percent in the first nine months of this year due to good sales of its major product, high-quality cement.
